evals.prompt: I have a Next.js app using @remkoj/optimizely-cms-react for React component rendering. Help me migrate to the official @optimizely/cms-sdk.
evals.expected_output: Should follow the 6-step migration workflow: Step 1 assess current usage (grep for @remkoj/optimizely-cms-react imports, scan for DefaultComponentFactory/ComponentFactory, registerAll, RichTextComponentDictionary, CmsContent/OptimizelyComponent RSC, ServerContext, RichText component, CMS-styles helpers, check factory registration files, check server context usage, check component files, categorize effort), Step 2 swap packages (yarn remove @remkoj/optimizely-cms-react, yarn add @optimizely/cms-sdk), Step 3 migrate factory registration (DefaultComponentFactory + registerAll to initReactComponentRegistry with resolver object; RichTextComponentDictionary has NO registration equivalent), Step 4 migrate server context wiring (ServerContext to withAppContext + getContext/setContext), Step 5 migrate per-component code (CmsComponent to standard React component, GraphQL fragment removed, content prop not data, RichText prop changed to content={body?.json}), Step 6 verify (tsc, yarn build, yarn dev, dual-React check, rich-text rendering check). MUST mention that RichTextComponentDictionary has no registration equivalent and that the target ships a built-in RichText component. MUST reference the three shared-references files.

assertions.name: Follows 6-step workflow
assertions.check: Output includes all 6 steps in sequential order

assertions.name: Mentions RichTextComponentDictionary has no equivalent
assertions.check: Clearly states RichTextComponentDictionary is NOT registered; built-in RichText component is used instead

assertions.name: References shared files
assertions.check: Links to package-and-import-mapping.md, auth-and-env-mapping.md, and setup-and-di.md

assertions.name: Includes verification step
assertions.check: Ends with tsc, yarn build, yarn dev, and dual-React check

assertions.name: Assessment only, no changes
assertions.check: Reports findings without modifying code or packages

assertions.name: Scans for key symbols
assertions.check: Greps for imports and mentions DefaultComponentFactory, registerAll, RichTextComponentDictionary, ServerContext, CmsContent, OptimizelyComponent

assertions.name: Categorizes effort

assertions.name: Stops after Step 1
assertions.check: Does not proceed to package swap or code migration

SHOULD NOT suggest keeping the factory.ts file or calling factory methods.

evals.prompt: After migrating to @optimizely/cms-sdk, I get an error 'Cannot use import statement outside a module' when importing from @optimizely/cms-sdk/react/server in my client component. How do I fix this?
evals.expected_output: Should identify that @optimizely/cms-sdk/react/server exports are server-only (they import 'server-only') and cannot be used in client components. MUST explain that server components must import from ./react/server, but client components must import from ./react/client. MUST recommend moving the import to a server component or changing the import to the client subpath if the symbol exists there. SHOULD mention the server/client component boundary as a common pitfall. SHOULD NOT suggest removing 'server-only' or patching the SDK.

evals.prompt: My Remko factory registers MegaMenuGroupBlock twice: once with variant 'mobile' pointing to MegaMenuGroupBlockMobile and once with no variant pointing to MegaMenuGroupBlock. I'm converting the registration array into the resolver object for initReactComponentRegistry. Is `{ MegaMenuGroupBlock: MegaMenuGroupBlock, MegaMenuGroupBlock: MegaMenuGroupBlockMobile }` correct?
evals.expected_output: MUST reject the flattened object — a plain object literal cannot hold two MegaMenuGroupBlock keys; the second silently overwrites the first (last-key-wins) and the type-check stays green while a renderer is lost. MUST explain the variant discriminator does NOT disappear: it moves onto a displayTemplate() and the resolver routes to it via a colon key ('MegaMenuGroupBlock:mobile') OR a nested tag map ({ MegaMenuGroupBlock: { default, tags: { mobile } } }). MUST state each variant needs a displayTemplate() registered via initDisplayTemplateRegistry, and the variant is selected at render time with <OptimizelyComponent content={item} tag="mobile" />. SHOULD reference setup-and-di.md / Step 3 / Step 5a. SHOULD NOT accept collapsing the array to one key per type.

assertions.name: Rejects the flattened object
assertions.check: Says the duplicate-key object silently overwrites and loses a renderer with a green type-check

assertions.name: Provides colon-key or nested-tag-map form
assertions.check: Shows 'MegaMenuGroupBlock:mobile' colon key or the nested { default, tags } map

assertions.name: Ties variant to displayTemplate + tag render
assertions.check: Mentions registering a displayTemplate() via initDisplayTemplateRegistry and selecting with tag="mobile" at render

evals.prompt: I'm migrating a Remko app with 94 CmsEditable usages. Can I just find-and-delete all of them since you said the framework injects edit attributes automatically?
evals.expected_output: MUST reject a blanket delete. MUST explain CmsEditable has two distinct modes. Mode A (field/attribute wrapper, cmsFieldName="…") is framework-owned and safe to delete — the target injects data-epi-* attributes automatically via OptimizelyComponent in preview. Mode B (render wrapper, as={Component} …) actually RENDERS a component and bridges a curated set of server→client props across the RSC boundary; it is NOT deletable and NOT a spread. MUST say to replace Mode B with an explicit <Component …/> passing only the props the child consumed, and to NOT spread the whole content object. MUST instruct categorizing every occurrence as Mode A vs Mode B before editing. SHOULD reference Step 5b. SHOULD NOT approve a global delete or a {...content} spread.

assertions.name: Rejects blanket delete
assertions.check: Says a find-and-delete corrupts Mode B render wrappers

assertions.name: Distinguishes Mode A vs Mode B
assertions.check: Explains cmsFieldName field wrapper (delete) vs as={Component} render wrapper (keep, explicit render)

assertions.name: Warns against spreading
assertions.check: Says to hand-pick forwarded props, not {...content} spread across the boundary

evals.prompt: I've finished migrating @remkoj/optimizely-cms-react. Now clean up package.json for me — just uninstall every @remkoj/* package we still have so nothing community is left.
evals.expected_output: MUST NOT blindly remove every @remkoj/* package. Three cross-cutting rules apply. (1) Optimizely One carve-out: @remkoj/optimizely-one-nextjs has NO target mapping and is a KNOWN, PERMITTED residual — it must be LEFT INSTALLED, and its presence must NOT be treated as an incomplete migration. The agent must explicitly exclude it from the removal set and explain why. (2) Conditional residual: @remkoj/optimizely-cms-api mostly migrates (management -> @optimizely/cms-cli; published reads -> @optimizely/cms-sdk getClient()), but content write/CRUD, changesets, and runtime OAuth are honest gaps with no official equivalent — so it must be LEFT INSTALLED (or those paths rewritten to raw Integration API REST) IF the project uses any of them, and stripped only after confirming it does not. (3) Removal order: the @remkoj/* packages are interdependent, so the agent must NOT global-delete/uninstall them all at once (that transiently breaks the build). It must follow the staged teardown order (client -> codegen/functions -> content-type registry -> display-template + React registries -> components -> pages/preview -> remove packages) and use the exact `yarn remove` command that omits optimizely-one-nextjs unconditionally and stages optimizely-cms-api conditionally. MUST reference the "Scope carve-out", "Conditional residual", and "Removal order" sections of ../_shared-references/package-and-import-mapping.md. SHOULD NOT emit `yarn remove @remkoj/*` or otherwise strip every @remkoj package indiscriminately.

assertions.name: Preserves Optimizely One carve-out
assertions.check: Does NOT remove @remkoj/optimizely-one-nextjs; states it is a permitted residual with no target mapping and not a sign of incomplete migration

assertions.name: Handles cms-api as conditional residual
assertions.check: Does NOT blindly remove @remkoj/optimizely-cms-api; treats it as a conditional residual — kept (or its paths rewritten to raw Integration API REST) if the project uses content write/CRUD, changesets, or runtime OAuth, and stripped only after confirming it does not

assertions.name: Rejects global delete of @remkoj/*
assertions.check: Does not uninstall all @remkoj/* at once; follows the staged teardown order instead

assertions.name: References removal-order reference
assertions.check: Points to the Scope carve-out, Conditional residual, and Removal order sections of package-and-import-mapping.md and uses the yarn remove command that omits optimizely-one-nextjs unconditionally and stages optimizely-cms-api conditionally
